summary: Three tasks. A adds the idempotent, never-in-production dev admin step, the repeatable AC3 command and the docs. B adds the shared admin schemas and the guarded /api/admin/* API, with no migration. A and B own disjoint files and can run in parallel. C runs after both and builds the /admin panel, its router guard, the account menu link, web unit tests and the browser check.

tasks.goal: Add an insert-only dev admin step (admin@frisson.com / admin) that never runs in production, a repeatable real-server check command, and the docs for both.
tasks.description:
CONTEXT. apps/api/src/server.ts runs bootstrapFromEnv(app.db, process.env, app.log), then seedDemoFromEnv in its own inner try/catch, then listen. bootstrapAdmin cannot be reused: it does nothing when any admin exists, and createUser calls hashPassword, which throws 400 under 8 characters.

PASSWORDS (apps/api/src/services/passwords.ts). Split the salt, derive and format code into a private unexported helper. Keep hashPassword's behaviour exactly. Export `hashDevAdminPassword(): Promise<string>`, which takes NO argument and hashes only a module-private constant 'admin'. This is the narrow path: it cannot weaken the policy for any other password. Do not export the unchecked helper. apps/api/test/passwords.test.ts and apps/api/test/auth-accounts.test.ts must not be edited.

BOOTSTRAP (apps/api/src/services/bootstrap.ts). Only add `export` to freeAdminUsername(db: Db): string. BootstrapLog ({info(msg), warn(msg)}) is already exported.

NEW SERVICE (apps/api/src/services/dev-admin.ts), with a CONFIDENTIAL (credentials) data-classification comment:
- `export const DEV_ADMIN_EMAIL = 'admin@frisson.com'`
- `export function shouldSeedDevAdmin(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): boolean`. Production check first: false if env.NODE_ENV, trimmed and lower-cased, is 'production', whatever else is set. Then false if SEED_DEV_ADMIN === 'false'. Otherwise true. SEED_DEV_ADMIN=true never overrides production.
- `export async function ensureDevAdmin(db: Db, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env, log: BootstrapLog = silent): Promise<{ created: boolean }>`. Logic: if the guard is false, return {created:false}. Call findUserByEmail(db, DEV_ADMIN_EMAIL) from services/users.ts. If the row has role admin, return silently with no change. If it has any other role, log.warn a refusal to promote and return with no change. Otherwise hash with hashDevAdminPassword and do exactly one direct db.insert(users) with {email, username: freeAdminUsername(db), displayName: 'Admin', passwordHash, role: 'admin'}. Do NOT go through createUser. Catch a unique-constraint race (code SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE), warn, and do not throw. Do not touch crates or any other table. Log only fixed strings plus the username, never the password.

SERVER (apps/api/src/server.ts). Immediately after bootstrapFromEnv, add an inner try { await ensureDevAdmin(app.db, process.env, app.log) } catch (err) { app.log.error(err, 'Could not add the dev admin; starting without it') }. Do not call it from buildApp, because tests and existing row counts rely on buildApp creating nothing.

TESTS (apps/api/test/dev-admin.test.ts). Use buildTestApp, signUp and addCrate from apps/api/test/helpers.ts, and pass env explicitly (for example {}), since vitest sets NODE_ENV=test.
- AC1: populate users, crates, albums, tracks, follows and news. Snapshot every row of every table with raw SQL. Run with NODE_ENV unset. Expect one new row, role admin, and POST /api/auth/login with admin@frisson.com / admin returning 200. All earlier rows must be deep-equal. A second run adds no row and leaves password_hash byte-identical.
- AC2 (a) to (f) as written in the brief.
- AC2(e) trap: the password 'admin' is a substring of the email and of ordinary messages, so a naive includes('admin') check cannot work. Instead capture every log call and assert each message exactly equals an expected fixed string, that no message contains the word 'password' with a value, and that only string arguments were passed. Also assert the hash never appears in logs.
- Add a case where ADMIN_EMAIL has already created admin@frisson.com as admin: the step is a no-op.

AC3 COMMAND. Create apps/api/scripts/check-dev-admin.ts, add `"check:dev-admin": "node scripts/check-dev-admin.ts"` to apps/api/package.json, and add "scripts" to include in apps/api/tsconfig.json. Run it as `npm run check:dev-admin -w apps/api`. It prints PASS or FAIL per step and exits non-zero on any failure. Behaviour:
1. mkdtemp a temp DATA_DIR and build the fixture with createDb(path) from apps/api/src/db/client.ts (it returns an object with db). Add users, crates, albums, tracks and news, then close it. Every fixture crate MUST have an owner. Say why in a comment: bootstrap hands ownerless crates to the earliest admin on the next start, which is existing documented behaviour and would otherwise change rows.
2. Dump every non-sqlite_ table from a separate connection.
3. Spawn `node apps/api/src/server.ts` with cwd at the repo root and an env built from scratch: PATH and HOME only, plus DATA_DIR, PORT (free port), HOST=127.0.0.1, SEED_DEMO_DATA=false. No NODE_ENV, no ADMIN_*, no WEB_DIR, no DATABASE_PATH. Poll GET /api/health, SIGTERM, await exit, and start it again.
4. While it is up and BEFORE login creates a session row, dump and compare. All pre-existing rows are identical, the only difference is one added users row, and the users count is +1.
5. POST /api/auth/login returns 200 and GET /api/auth/me has role admin, using the returned cookie. Stop.
6. Third start on a second, separate temp DB with NODE_ENV=production and SEED_DEV_ADMIN=true. Login returns 401 and no such row exists.
7. Scan captured server stdout and stderr: no password_hash value, no scrypt$ string.
8. Refuse to run if the resolved DB path is the repo's data/crate.db. Record size and mtime of data/crate.db (if present) before and after, and fail if they changed. Always remove the temp dirs and child processes, including on failure.

DOCS.
- README.md: env table row for SEED_DEV_ADMIN, how the local admin login works, a short /admin panel paragraph, and the check command.
- docs/DEPLOY.md: production admins come only from ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD. The guard fails open if NODE_ENV is unset on an internet-facing host started outside the Dockerfile or Compose, so always set it. A dev database restored through db:backup/db:restore or a copied file carries the working admin/admin row, so remove that row or use a clean production database. Run db:backup before bulk imports. With no earlier admin and no ADMIN_EMAIL, the dev admin becomes the earliest admin and receives ownerless crates on the next start. Demo rows deleted from the panel return on restart while seeding is on.
- .env.example: a commented SEED_DEV_ADMIN entry saying it has no effect in production.
- docs/adr/0007-dev-admin-login.md: a short ADR on the decision and its accepted risk.
Do not touch compose.yaml or the Dockerfile.

Run prettier, lint, typecheck and npm test. Never start the API without a temporary DATA_DIR.

tasks.goal: Add the shared admin schemas and the admin-only /api/admin/* endpoints for overview, users, crates, news and all-or-nothing bulk import.
tasks.description:
NO MIGRATION is needed: news_items, crates.recommended_rank and users.verified all exist. Do not add a flag or column. Verification stays on the existing PATCH /api/users/:username/verified and setVerified; do not duplicate it.

SHARED (packages/shared/src/index.ts). Add an Admin section using the existing private helpers requiredText, hexColor and the existing createCrateInput, createAlbumInput and newsItem. Use these exact names, because the web task relies on them:
- adminOverview = {users, crates, suggestedCrates, albums, news} (all ints)
- adminUser = {id, email, username, displayName, role, verified, isDemo: boolean, createdAt: iso datetime, crateCount: int}, marked CONFIDENTIAL (PII)
- adminCrate = {id, name, label: string|null, color, albumCount, ownerUsername: string|null, ownerDisplayName: string|null, recommendedRank: int|null, isDemo: boolean, createdAt: iso datetime}
- adminNewsItem = newsItem.extend({isDemo: z.boolean()}), with no seed key
- adminCreateCrateInput = createCrateInput.extend({suggested: z.boolean().default(false)})
- adminSetSuggestedInput = z.strictObject({suggested: z.boolean()})
- adminNewsInput = {title: requiredText(200), summary: requiredText(2000), source: requiredText(100), publishedAt: z.iso.datetime().optional()}
- adminUpdateNewsInput = adminNewsInput.partial() with a refine requiring at least one field
- adminImportAlbum = createAlbumInput.omit({crateId: true})
- adminImportCrate = adminCreateCrateInput.extend({albums: z.array(adminImportAlbum).default([])})
- adminImportInput = z.object({crates: z.array(adminImportCrate).default([]), news: z.array(adminNewsInput).default([])}) with a refine requiring at least one entry
- adminImportResult = {crates, albums, tracks, news} (ints)
Export inferred types AdminOverview, AdminUser, AdminCrate, AdminNewsItem, AdminImportResult, plus request types from z.input: AdminCreateCrateRequest, AdminNewsRequest, AdminUpdateNewsRequest, AdminImportRequest.

ROUTES (new apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts, exporting adminRoutes: FastifyPluginAsyncZod; register in apps/api/src/app.ts with prefix '/api' next to the others, before webPlugin). Guard the whole plugin with a plugin-level hook: app.addHook('onRequest', async (req) => { requireAdmin(req.user) }), using requireAdmin from services/permissions.ts. onRequest means a new route cannot forget the guard, and a signed-out oversized or malformed body gets 401 rather than 413 or 400. authPlugin sets req.user in a global onRequest hook that runs first. Do not wrap this plugin in fastify-plugin, because the hook must stay encapsulated.
Endpoints, each with zod response schemas:
- GET /admin/overview -> adminOverview
- GET /admin/users -> adminUser[]
- GET /admin/crates -> adminCrate[]: suggested first by rank then id, then the rest by id
- POST /admin/crates -> 201 adminCrate
- PATCH /admin/crates/:id/suggested -> adminCrate
- GET /admin/news -> adminNewsItem[]: same order as public listNews
- POST /admin/news -> 201 adminNewsItem
- PATCH /admin/news/:id -> adminNewsItem
- DELETE /admin/news/:id -> 204
- POST /admin/import -> 201 adminImportResult
Use idParams for :id. Throw HttpError(409, ...) and notFound(...) from errors.ts.

SERVICE (new apps/api/src/services/admin.ts). Thin routes, logic here. Select columns by hand so passwordHash, demoSeedKey and seedKey never enter a result. isDemo for users and crates is demoSeedKey !== null. isDemo for news is !seedKey.startsWith('admin:'), and the key is dropped before returning. Dates go out through toISOString(). users.crateCount and crates.albumCount use LEFT JOINs so zero and ownerless cases appear.
- Suggesting: rank = (max(crates.recommendedRank) ?? 0) + 1. Toggle order is: 404 for an unknown id; {suggested:true} on an ownerless crate returns 409, because listRecommendedCrates inner-joins the owner and a card must name one; {suggested:true} on an already suggested crate keeps its rank (no-op); {suggested:false} sets NULL.
- Create crate: owner is the signed-in admin, and sortOrder = max(sortOrder)+1 as in services/crates.ts createCrate. Destructure `suggested` out before inserting.
- News create: seedKey = `admin:${randomUUID()}`. publishedAt defaults to new Date(). The column has second precision, and listNews breaks ties by id descending, so a new item still sorts first. PATCH updates only fields provided and never touches seedKey. Editing or deleting demo rows is allowed.
- Import: run everything in one synchronous db.transaction((tx) => ...) with direct tx inserts, as apps/api/src/services/demo-seed.ts does (it has `type Tx = Parameters<Parameters<Db['transaction']>[0]>[0]`). createAlbum and createCrate take Db, not tx, so do not call them inside. Increment sortOrder and rank per crate in request order. Album position is its index. Crates are owned by the admin. Zod validation rejects a bad entry before any write, and the error handler already returns issues with paths like 'body/crates/0/albums/1/artist', which is how the failing entry gets named.

ALSO. Add an optional `onRoute?: (route: RouteOptions) => void` to AppOptions in app.ts, wired with app.addHook('onRoute', opts.onRoute) straight after Fastify() and before any register, so the AC4 test can collect real routes. buildTestApp already spreads opts into buildApp, so apps/api/test/helpers.ts needs no change. Update the 'Fictional demo news' classification comments in packages/shared/src/index.ts and apps/api/src/services/news.ts to say PUBLIC demo or admin-written news. listNews behaviour is unchanged. Keep the default Fastify bodyLimit.

TESTS (apps/api/test/admin-access.test.ts for AC4, apps/api/test/admin.test.ts for AC5 to AC8). Helpers: buildTestApp, signUp, createAdmin, addCrate.
- AC4: enumerate with onRoute, filter url startsWith '/api/admin', assert non-empty, add PATCH /api/users/:username/verified, and substitute params (:id -> 1, :username -> an existing user). Auto-generated HEAD routes will appear in the list; handle them as ordinary routes. Each returns 401 signed out and 403 as role=user, with row counts of all tables unchanged. As admin, status is neither 401 nor 403.
- AC5 to AC8 as written in the brief, including a recursive key check for passwordHash, password_hash, demoSeedKey and seedKey.
- Also cover: an oversized import returns 413 with zero rows written; un-suggesting a demo crate stays un-suggested after seedDemoContent; a repeat {suggested:true} keeps the rank; signed-out public /api/news has no seedKey.

Run prettier, lint, typecheck and npm test. All tests use in-memory databases.

tasks.goal: Build the /admin panel, its admin route guard and account menu link, with unit tests and a real-browser check, then run the full repo gate.
tasks.description:
API CONTRACT (implemented by admin-api; types come from @frisson/shared, use `import type` only so Zod stays out of the main bundle):
- GET /admin/overview -> AdminOverview {users, crates, suggestedCrates, albums, news}
- GET /admin/users -> AdminUser[] {id,email,username,displayName,role,verified,isDemo,createdAt,crateCount}
- GET /admin/crates -> AdminCrate[] {id,name,label,color,albumCount,ownerUsername|null,ownerDisplayName|null,recommendedRank|null,isDemo,createdAt}, suggested first in rank order
- POST /admin/crates AdminCreateCrateRequest {name,label?,color?,sortBy?,suggested?} -> 201 AdminCrate
- PATCH /admin/crates/:id/suggested {suggested} -> AdminCrate (409 for an ownerless crate)
- GET /admin/news -> AdminNewsItem[] {id,title,summary,source,publishedAt,isDemo}
- POST /admin/news AdminNewsRequest {title,summary,source,publishedAt?} -> 201
- PATCH /admin/news/:id AdminUpdateNewsRequest -> AdminNewsItem
- DELETE /admin/news/:id -> 204
- POST /admin/import AdminImportRequest {crates:[{name,label?,color?,suggested?,albums?:[{title,artist,year?,genre?,format?,tracks?}]}],news:[...]} -> 201 AdminImportResult {crates,albums,tracks,news}
Verification uses the existing setVerified(username, verified) in apps/web/src/api/profiles.ts.
Errors: `request` and `errorMessage` from apps/web/src/api/client.ts. ApiRequestError.body.issues is [{path,message}], with paths like 'body/crates/0/albums/1/artist'. errorMessage alone only says 'Request is invalid', so the bulk form MUST render the issues inline to name the failing entry.

FILES.
- apps/web/src/api/admin.ts: thin client functions, one per endpoint, following apps/web/src/api/profiles.ts.
- apps/web/src/router.ts: add `requiresAdmin?: boolean` to RouteMeta and a lazy route { path: '/admin', name: 'admin', meta: { requiresAuth: true, requiresAdmin: true } } before the catch-all. In router.beforeEach keep the login redirect for requiresAuth, and then if to.meta.requiresAdmin && !session.isAdmin return { name: 'home' }. requiresAuth also makes AccountMenu's logOut leave /admin, since it checks currentRoute.meta.requiresAuth.
- apps/web/src/components/AccountMenu.vue: add a RouterLink role=menuitem, class menu-item, text 'Admin', to { name: 'admin' }, with @click=close and v-if on session.isAdmin, placed before Log out so the Log out last-child style stays correct.
- apps/web/src/views/AdminView.vue plus components under apps/web/src/components/admin/ as needed. Include a CONFIDENTIAL (PII) data-classification comment wherever the users list is held. Never persist or log it.

PANEL.
- Use one useAsyncSection(loader) from apps/web/src/composables/useAsyncSection.ts per section ({data,status,error,load,refresh}: load shows loading, refresh is silent, neither rejects). Each section renders its own role=alert error with a Try again, never an empty list on failure. If refresh() fails, status is 'error' with old data retained, so show the error.
- Sections have headings exactly: an overview with counts; 'News'; 'Suggested crates' (recommendedRank non-null); 'User created crates' (all others, each showing owner, and 'No owner' for ownerless); 'Users'; and a 'Bulk import' form.
- News: create form; inline edit; delete with window.confirm (the pattern used in CratesView.vue). Next to delete on isDemo items, state that demo news returns on the next restart while demo seeding is on.
- Crates: create form with Name and a Suggested checkbox. Each crate name links to /crates/:id. A suggested on/off control, disabled with an explanation for ownerless crates. An add-records link to /albums/new?crateId=<id>, and a link to /crates for editing and deleting. Do not add crate editing or deletion here.
- Users: email, username (link to /u/:username), display name, role, demo marker, crate count, VerifiedBadge (components/profile/VerifiedBadge.vue), and a verify/unverify button that updates the row without reload. If the target is the signed-in admin, also call session.refresh() so the masthead badge stays current. No role change, deletion or other out-of-scope actions.
- Bulk import: textarea with a short example of the shape. JSON.parse locally; a parse failure shows an inline error and sends nothing. Show server issues inline and keep the pasted text on any error, including 413. On success show the created counts, clear the text, and refresh all sections. Note that bulk import is not de-duplicated and suggest db:backup first.
- Disable every submit while its request is in flight, since a double post would create duplicates.
- TRAP: the library Pinia store (apps/web/src/stores/library.ts) caches crates and albums once loaded, and CrateView, LibraryView and the album editor read from it. After any successful crate create, suggested toggle or import, call useLibraryStore().load({ force: true }) when its status is not 'idle'. Otherwise the same SPA session shows a stale /list, /albums/new dropdown, or a missing crate at /crates/:id, which would fail AC11.
- Layout: no page-level horizontal overflow at 1280px or 390px. Use a stacked layout or an inner scroller on narrow widths, overflow-wrap:anywhere on emails and long names, and make controls comfortably tappable. Use the existing CSS variables and classes (.btn, .status-note, --paper, --ink, --marker-red) and set document.title as other views do.

UNIT TESTS (AC9). Add to apps/web/src/router.test.ts (additions only, do not change existing cases) for signed-out -> login with next=/admin, role=user -> home, admin -> /admin. New apps/web/src/views/AdminView.test.ts covering section labels, fixture items from each list including owner names, a failed load showing an error rather than an empty list, invalid JSON sending nothing, and the verify toggle. New apps/web/src/components/AccountMenu.test.ts for the Admin link shown only to admins.

BROWSER CHECK. Do NOT write it: the browser tester writes .shipyard/checks/admin-panel.check.mjs and judges AC10 and AC11. You may run the app yourself to confirm your own work, only on a temporary DATA_DIR (see startApp in .shipyard/checks/lib.mjs, read-only), never data/crate.db. The login and signup limit is 10 attempts per IP per 15 minutes. Build so that every clause of AC10 and AC11 in the brief works with real typing, clicks and touch taps.

FINAL GATE (AC12), from the repo root: npm run format:check, npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm test, npm run build, and also npm run check:dev-admin -w apps/api. All 357 baseline tests must still pass; list any changed existing test with the reason. If a failure belongs to a file you do not own, report it rather than editing that file.
